title: Capacity Safety Layers & Burst Override: Predictive Preemption and Decaying-Credit Policy PRD
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers with Dedicated capacity sometimes experience noisy neighbor effects and unexpected latency spikes during transient workload surges. Existing approaches (static guarded lanes, simple preemption) either over-throttle legitimate bursts or allow tail-latency to degrade SLOs. This PRD proposes a layered safety model that combines predictive preemption windows, a decaying-credit burst override for tenants, and an operator-visible guardband to balance availability and fairness. The goal is to provide deterministic degradation semantics for Dedicated customers and allow controlled, auditable temporary capacity overrides with automatic decay and rollback.
scope: In-scope: policy DSL for safety layers; tenant-level decaying credit ledger; predictive preemption window computed from recent trace percentiles; runtime hooks to enforce soft-eviction and graceful fallback to hosted model variants; observability dashboards and alerting; operator override API with audit logs. Out-of-scope: changes to cloud provider allocation primitives, long-term financial billing model changes, UI redesign of Console beyond a single admin panel for overrides.
goals: Define a composable policy model for Dedicated capacity safety layers that operators and customers can reason about
Implement a tenant decaying-credit system that grants time-bound burst overrides that automatically decay and expire
Add predictive preemption windows using 95/99 token latency and queue depth trends to avoid reactive mass-eviction
Provide end-to-end observability: per-tenant credit state, safety-layer triggers, and SLA impact metrics
Ship operator audit and rollback controls plus safety checks for Private/VPC deployments
non_goals: Rewrite the autoscaler or scheduler core (this work will integrate with existing autoscale hooks)
Introduce new billing primitives or price changes for burst credits
Full multi-region resharding or cross-zone live migration
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: When enabled in a staging cluster, the policy DSL can be deployed and evaluated in dry-run mode without evicting any traffic
AC-2: Decaying-credit grants are visible in the Console and can be consumed by tenant traffic for at least 30s and no more than configured TTL; credits decay linearly by default
AC-3: Predictive preemption prevents >80% of reactive mass-evictions observed during synthetic surge tests compared to baseline (no predictive window)
AC-4: In an orchestrated canary (5% traffic), automatic rollback triggers if p99 latency increases by >15% or error-rate delta >1% within 10 minutes
AC-5: Operator override actions are recorded in audit logs with user, timestamp, reason, and revert action; testable via sample audit query
AC-6: Metrics for tenant credit consumption, safety-layer activations, and fallback counts are emitted to Redwood telemetry and visible on the dedicated-capacity dashboard
architecture_overview: Three-layer approach: (1) Safety Band (configurable soft limits per pool/tenant) evaluated continuously; (2) Predictive Window computed from short-term latency and queue trend models to preemptively throttle or shift non-critical requests; (3) Burst Override Ledger that tracks per-tenant credits (grants, consumption, decay) and allows temporary priority increases. Enforcement is implemented as lightweight runtime filters in the request path with asynchronous reconciliation to the scheduler. Operator APIs expose manual grants and forced-eviction with strong guards.
implementation_plan: Spec API: policy DSL and UI contracts (week 1-2)
Runtime: implement filters for safety-band checks and credit lookup in serving runtime (week 3-6)
Ledger: lightweight Redis-backed per-tenant ledger with TTL and decay worker (week 4-6)
Predictive model: simple rolling-percentile + linear trend detector service (week 3-5)
Observability: telemetry events, dashboard panels, and alert rules (week 5-7)
Canary & rollout: staged rollout with dry-run, 5% beta, 25% ramp, full launch (week 8-12)
Docs & runbook: operator runbook, SRE playbook, customer-facing PRD summary (week 9-12)
telemetry_and_metrics: SLO impact: p50/p95/p99 latency delta vs baseline, error rate delta
rollout_plan: Alpha (internal): enable dry-run policies + ledger visibility in a staging Dedicated cluster; collect telemetry and tune decay parameters
Beta (customers opt-in): allow 3 customers on Dedicated to test grantable credits and observe behavior; SRE to monitor and maintain rollback playbook
GA: enabled by default with conservative defaults and opt-out toggle; document expected degradations and customer notifications
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Credits could be abused to bypass tenancy isolation. Mitigation: rate limits on grants, per-customer quotas, and operator approval gate for cross-tenant grants.
Risk: Predictive model false positives throttle legitimate traffic. Mitigation: start with conservative thresholds, dry-run telemetry, and fast rollback triggers.
Risk: Ledger consistency under partition. Mitigation: design ledger for eventual consistency with local caches and reconciliation windows; surface mismatch alerts to SRE.
notes: Design choice: linear decay chosen for predictability; alternative exponential decay considered but rejected due to harder customer expectations
We will expose a conservative default credit TTL of 60s and default grant sizes of 1-3 credits worth ~500 concurrent tokens each for initial beta
Coordination required with billing only if customer wants permanent purchase of credits (out of scope for this PRD)
